objective: Make Vesper feel like a polished, accessible, expressive visual novel reader while retaining engine-neutral external authoring; conclude with one original showcase game using freshly generated assets.

rules.architecture: All Rust/Bevy systems and widgets generic; narrative/assets/themes externally authored. Preserve backward compatibility for existing example directories and save schema or provide explicit migrations.
rules.player_vs_author: Player preferences override game theme when explicitly selected, without editing source files; themes remain hot-reloadable for unoverridden options.
rules.performance: No slow I/O, art generation, blocking parsing or unbounded per-frame allocations on update/render threads; use asynchronous loading/writing and cache renderer assets.
rules.platform: Linux x86-64, Wayland/Hyprland first; keyboard-first with pointer support. No Mac hardware, paid API or npm requirement.
rules.verification: Each milestone earns its weight only after criteria are met on a passing source commit with targeted tests, screenshot evidence for visual work and full relevant CI; an accepted roadmap is not evidence of feature completion.
rules.visuals: Coherent visual language, contrast, legibility and controlled motion are more important than simply adding effects; default to readable/reduced-distraction behavior.
rules.production_scope: Exclude a WYSIWYG editor, AI at runtime, remote backends, full 3D renderer, general scripting-language replacement, and arbitrary game-specific engine branches.

showcase.title: The Post Office at the Edge of Dawn
showcase.tone: Cozy, whimsical storybook fantasy with charming expressive characters and a little mystery
showcase.story_seed: A tiny moth courier must deliver a letter addressed to a morning that has not yet happened; each stop on the waking sky changes what the letter means.
showcase.asset_strategy: Generate original art at VX10; produce original local/procedural WAV/OGG cues and license-safe fonts. Package only external media and scripts. Keep prompts, source/provenance notes and consistency checks with the game.
showcase.presentation_demo: Settings live preview, themed UI, selected choices, reveal speed, background/character transitions, idle motion, atmosphere, history/saves, accessibility and low-motion mode

tasks.description: Introduce validated, versioned local player preferences, separate from game-authored themes and story saves.
acceptance: Preferences are stored in an atomic, bounded, versioned JSON file under the platform-appropriate user data/config directory; no writes on the render/update thread.
Precedence is explicit: validated player override > externally authored theme > engine default. Choosing Reset returns to game defaults without modifying game files.
A missing, corrupt, unsupported or stale preferences file falls back safely; compatible older versions migrate without deleting saves.
Unit tests cover round-trip persistence, malformed values, absent fonts, game switching, precedence, and migrations.

tasks.description: An engine-owned, keyboard-first Settings screen for players to tune dialogue presentation in real time.
acceptance: From pause/main menus, players can adjust dialogue panel opacity (bounded 0.60–1.00), dialogue font size multiplier (0.80–1.60), choose an installed or game-approved font with safe fallback, and restore defaults.
A live preview displays speaker, long wrapped body, choices and hints; changing the settings updates existing UI entities without restarting, editing game TOML, or resetting story position.
Settings persist after restart and apply to both bundled examples; invalid or missing fonts restore a readable fallback without a crash.
All options use proper selectable Bevy UI controls, not concatenated strings; keyboard and pointer operation plus screenshots at 946×511, 800×600, 1280×720 and 1920×1080 pass.
Game theme changes under --watch continue to apply where a player has not overridden a value.

tasks.description: Replace string-built in-story choice selection with reusable selectable UI rows, and refine dialogue hierarchy.
acceptance: Each choice is a separate, engine-owned UI entity with selection/highlight, focus, mouse target and keyboard action; choice data remains supplied by external .vn scripts.
Speaker nameplate, body, controls hint and selection indicator have distinct, themeable geometry; no fixed giant text string synthesizes choice selection.
Long/multilingual dialogue and 2–9 options wrap without intersecting hints or viewport edges at 946×511, 955×520, 800×600, 900×700 and widescreen sizes.
F5/F9 preserves selection; pointer and keyboard interactions cannot double-activate or advance while a menu is open; screenshots and input regressions pass.

tasks.description: Authorable animated text reveal, controlled player reading speed and clear advance affordances.
acceptance: A reveal effect supports instant/off, slow, normal and fast player choices, with Unicode grapheme-safe pacing and no string corruption.
Enter/Space on revealing text finishes the current line before advancing; pause, menu, load, and history never accidentally skip; optional auto-advance is explicitly opt-in.
An unobtrusive themeable continue cue animates only when dialogue is complete; reduced-motion mode makes it static.
Reveal state reconstructs safely after save/load, hot reload and window resize, including restored completed lines; no frame-rate-dependent narrative execution.

tasks.description: Data-authored, reusable transitions and gentle camera motion without hardcoded game-specific cinematics.
acceptance: External theme/story data can specify bounded crossfade, fade-through-color and soft-slide background transitions, with compatible defaults for legacy .vn games.
An optional restrained 2D pan/zoom ('Ken Burns') preset preserves aspect, guards against image-edge exposure and never blocks keyboard input.
Transitions can be interrupted, skipped, paused, restored and hot-reloaded safely without leaving stale entities or black frames.
CI captures start/mid/end frames for two different external stories and proves each effect reaches its declared final visual state.

tasks.description: Better external sprite presentation: layers, anchors, expression changes and subtle, skippable motion.
acceptance: Externally declared sprite anchors/scale/depth and expression-crossfades work for multiple characters without engine references to specific games.
Bounded optional entrance/exit and gentle idle motion are presentation-only, deterministic under pause, disabled under reduced motion, and do not change story state.
Character positions remain legible behind dialogue and in narrow viewports, and layering is preserved through save/load and compatible hot reload.
Automated screenshot sequences verify z-order, anchor positions, expression transitions, pause behavior and reduced-motion behavior.

tasks.description: Subtle visual atmosphere, configurable UI polish, and unobtrusive interactive feedback.
acceptance: Provide a small, bounded data-driven library of 2D atmospheric presets such as drifting motes, gentle glow and vignette, with deterministic seeds and no mandatory shaders.
Themeable focus transitions, choice confirmation feedback and optional original UI cues are consistent across menus and choices.
Effects are optional, degrade gracefully with missing art/audio, stop or pause correctly, and have a reduced-motion/off setting.
Runtime effects use cached assets and bounded entity counts; no synchronous file I/O, image generation or expensive parsing runs on the update/render thread.

tasks.description: Make returning to a story more pleasant without compromising durable saves.
acceptance: A readable, scrollable dialogue backlog shows the current session's recent lines with speaker names and scene boundaries, with a documented bounded memory limit and no spoilers from future branches.
A structured load/save UI shows existing slot information and provides confirmation before overwrite; the existing F5/F9 quick actions remain backward compatible.
History, menus and save slots are keyboard-first and pointer-accessible; exiting preserves current story/choice state; no accidental dialogue progression.
Atomic background I/O and versioned saves continue working; old saves remain loadable or receive an explicit tested migration path.

tasks.description: Verify visual clarity, accessibility, settings reliability and Linux-first performance before the showcase game.
acceptance: Readable defaults and player controls for high-contrast text, reduced motion, text speed/instant reveal, and safe font fallback are documented and tested.

Screenshot tests isolate actual glyph bounds (not only shared letter pixels) at the previously failed 946×511 and 955×520 Wayland sizes, 800×600, 900×700, 1280×720 and 1920×1080; dialogue/hint and option regions maintain measurable separation.
End-to-end CI covers keyboard/pointer navigation, focus, pause, saves, preference persistence, hot reload, transition interruptions, both legacy fairy tales and relocatable Linux packaging.

Check that visual polish introduces no blocking asset/file operations on the render thread and no unbounded per-frame allocation/asset spawning; record qualitative graphical artifact review separately from automated checks.
Linux/Wayland-first operation and free tooling are retained; hardware-specific audio/driver behavior is not falsely certified by Xvfb.

tasks.description: Create and publish The Post Office at the Edge of Dawn, a complete new external visual novel that demonstrates the new presentation features rather than another placeholder demo.
acceptance: Create a self-contained examples/dawn-post-office/ with its own game.toml, authored .vn narrative, theme(s), asset manifest, README, artwork/audio directories and runnable Linux launcher; no game-specific Rust branches.

Author a coherent cozy fantasy story (~12–20 minutes of normal reading) about a tiny moth courier delivering an impossible letter across the waking sky; include >=3 named characters, >=5 illustrated locations, >=3 meaningful endings and at least one conditional payoff.

Generate original, consistent-looking artwork for >=5 backgrounds and >=9 transparent character/expression images, plus a coordinated UI treatment and original procedurally generated sound/music; validate transparency, dimensions, path safety, provenance and permitted asset rights. Use image generation during this milestone, not placeholder art or borrowed copyrighted media.

Demonstrate in natural narrative beats: player font/size/opacity preferences, individual choice UI, text pacing, scene transitions, sprite expression/idle motion, atmosphere, history, save/resume, and reduced-motion fallback.

Pass story/asset validation and all ending-path checks; capture and review actual Linux screenshots/video-frame sequences, verify game package runs without Rust installed, and update README with launch commands and controls.
Final main-branch CI must be fully green and the user-facing playthrough must be coherent and visually reviewed; no declaration of 100% based solely on generated image count.
